newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank says won't intervene in forex.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank says won't intervene in forex.

text.p: Taiwan central bank governor Sheu Yuan-dong said on Saturday the bank would not intervene in the island's foreign exchange market despite the recent sharp depreciation of the local dollar.
"Because the market's operation is normal, the rate of the Taiwan dollar will be decided by the supply and demand of the market," Sheu told a news conference.
The Taiwan dollar, plagued by a downturn in the island's stock market that triggered outflows of foreign funds, has fallen sharply against its U.S. counterpart in May.
"The Taiwan dollar began to show a clear depreciation due to foreign fund outflows," Sheu said.
Private analysts have said they expected the central bank to welcome the recent rate fall because such a downturn would boost the island's export-driven economy.
The Taiwan dollar was at T$27.865 against Friday's T$27.867 close with 45 minutes left in Saturday's shortened session.
